summary_html:
Ka(G): best fit 1.59×10⁸ M−1 · 95% CI [1.14×10⁸, 2.08×10⁸] M−1 (−28% / +31%)
Conditional on the entered inputs: best fit 2.81×10⁸ M−1 (weighted R² 0.9957) · 95% CI [1.52×10⁸, 4.50×10⁸] M−1 (−46% / +60%)
verdict_headline: The inputs together are further from their entered values than you stated
notes_html:
The data fit only with the inputs, taken together, further from their entered values than their stated uncertainties allow (q = 23.9, p < 0.001). The fit put the correction here: [Host]₀ −11.3 % (3.8 σ), Guest (titrant, whole series) +9.3 % (3.1 σ), Ka,dye +3.0 % (0.3 σ), [Dye]₀ +0.2 % (0.1 σ) — the data see only 2 combinations of these 4 inputs, so the correction landed where those combinations point. Check the values you entered for them. The interval assumes the shifts are real.
Each input with a stated uncertainty was free to move within the uncertainty you stated for it, which usually widens the interval. Each interval at the entered inputs is worked out from 12 data points and 3 fitted parameters, and no interval reaches further than the parameter bounds this fit was given. The replicates leave the noise law uncertain (share between 0.63 and 1); the interval of Ka(G) is widened about 1.3-fold to hold for every share they allow: it takes the variance of the estimate as 1.57 times what the scatter of the data alone implies.
Weighted R² counts each titration point by how precise the replicates show it to be; the R² under Fit Quality counts every point equally.
How to read this plot: the Reading this plot button above.

split_note: the interval holds rejected values; accepted ones come in separate stretches. See Ka confidence.
cut_note: The dotted line is the cut-off: every Ka whose curve lies above it is inside the interval.
cut_step_note: The dotted line is the cut-off: every Ka whose curve lies above it is inside the interval. Where the fit at a Ka has to hold a signal parameter at its bound, it gives up that parameter as well as Ka, so the test allows it a larger drop and the line steps down. The level named here is the one where every signal parameter is free.

tooltip:
The line is the best weighted R² any fit can reach at each Ka; the shaded band is the range of Ka the data support.
Where you stated an uncertainty for an input, a second line and band show what the data support once the inputs may move within it.
With two binding constants the last panel shows which pairs of them the data support together, at the inputs as entered.
Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, right-click for the full view.
